meta.label: Menstrual cups and discs
tradeoffLabels: easiest to use day to day
meta.attribution: Every option here is a reusable menstrual cup or reusable menstrual disc, meant to be emptied, rinsed and used again through a cycle; single-use cups and discs are a separate purchase and are not included. Period products, the wider comparison elsewhere in this catalogue, sets reusables against pads and tampons on cost and body safety; this page only compares the reusable internal devices against each other, on price and everyday ease of use, and leans on the FDA's and Health Canada's own device registers rather than brand claims wherever a register exists. In the United States a menstrual cup or disc is a Class II medical device under FDA regulation 884.5400, product code 'Cup, Menstrual' (HHE); some brands here hold their own FDA 510(k) clearance, decided case by case, and others are registered and listed under that same device type without filing their own 510(k), which current FDA data shows is also a legitimate route once a device type is established. Neither path is scored here as inherently safer. Price is the figure shown on the brand's own site on the date checked, before any temporary sale discount unless the note says otherwise. Fit, insertion and removal depend on individual anatomy, childbirth history and whether an IUD is fitted; the device's own instructions and a clinician, not this page, are the source for those questions. A used cup or disc is not included as a secondhand option, because every manufacturer here instructs against sharing one between people. Not medical advice. Reviewed 2026-08. Suggest changes via Contribute.

reads.text: Compare menstrual cups and discs by everyday access, cost, body safety, and labor and sourcing.

criteria.label: Ease of use, fit options, and availability

products.name: DivaCup

economical.note: DivaCup's own site lists the Model 2 cup at $35.00.

accessibility.note: DivaCup sells three sizes (Model 0, 1, 2) and the largest has a molded easy-to-grip base for removal; the product page also carries visible fill lines and an air-hole rim design meant to help form a seal.

health.note: FDA's 510(k) database lists K021356, Diva International Inc., 'THE DIVACUP MENSTRUAL SOLUTION', decided substantially equivalent on 2002-07-16 under product code HHE. The product page states the cup is 100% medical-grade silicone with no added BPA, latex, dyes, or plastics.

ethics.note: B Lab's Certified B Corporation directory page for Diva International Inc. lists an overall B Impact Score of 121.2, above the 80-point minimum required for certification.

products.description: A three-size silicone cup with a molded stem base, individually FDA-cleared since 2002 and made by a Certified B Corporation.

products.name: Mooncup Original

economical.note: Mooncup's own site prices the Mooncup Original at 23.50 pounds.

accessibility.note: Two sizes are sold: Size A for age 30 or over or vaginal childbirth, Size B otherwise; both share a 21mm stem that can be trimmed for comfort.

health.note: FDA's 510(k) database lists two clearances for this cup: K040335 (Mooncup, LLC, decided 2005-03-30) and K060852 (Mooncup Limited, decided 2006-12-26), both product code HHE. The brand's own product page states the cup is medical-grade silicone (quartz and sandstone), latex-free, with no dyes, BPA, PFAS, phthalates, petroleum plastic or bleaches.

ethics.note: B Lab's Certified B Corporation directory page, now listed under Sisters Ltd after Mooncup's 2023 acquisition by &SISTERS, shows an overall B Impact Score of 147.5 against a median of 50.9 for ordinary businesses that complete the assessment.

products.description: A two-size UK silicone cup, individually FDA-cleared, from a Certified B Corporation with one of the higher B Impact scores in period care.

products.name: Lunette Period Cup

economical.note: Lunette's own site prices the clear Period Cup at 29.90 euros, tax included.

accessibility.note: Two sizes are sold, Size 1 for light to medium flow and Size 2 for medium to heavy flow, with no further fit customization offered.

health.note: FDA's 510(k) database lists K091754, Lune Group Ltd., 'LUNETTE MENSTRUAL CUP, MODELS 1 AND 2', decided substantially equivalent on 2009-11-13 under product code HHE. The brand's product page states the cup is 100% medical-grade silicone, free of BPA and latex.

products.description: A two-size Finnish silicone cup, individually FDA-cleared in 2009 and sold across Europe and the US.

products.name: MeLuna Classic/Sport

economical.note: MeLuna USA's site lists starter kits, which bundle a cup with accessories, at about $54 to $71.50 depending on what is included; this is a bundle price rather than a single-cup price, so it is not directly comparable to the single-unit prices scored for other brands here.

accessibility.note: MeLuna sells four handle styles (ball, stem, ring, no handle), three lengths and two firmness levels; the brand runs an interactive quiz to help a buyer choose the combination, which means more precise fit once decided but more decisions before a first purchase than most cups here.

health.note: FDA's 510(k) database lists K140626, Meluna, 'MELUNA CLASSIC/SPORT MENSTRUAL CUP', decided substantially equivalent on 2014-07-10 under product code HHE. MeLuna's own materials page states the cup is made of medical-grade TPE (thermoplastic elastomer) rather than silicone, certified BfR, FDA, 2002/72/EC and ISO 10993-10, and that the TPE contains no latex.

products.description: A German cup made of TPE rather than silicone, sold in four handle styles, three lengths and two firmness levels, so choosing one usually means using the brand's fit quiz first.

products.name: FemmyCycle

health.note: FDA's 510(k) database lists K121857, Femcap Incorporated, 'FEMMYCYCLE', decided substantially equivalent on 2012-11-15 under product code HHE.

products.description: A US cup individually FDA-cleared in 2012; price and design detail could not be confirmed from a source that was not a ranked retail or review listing, so only its clearance record is scored here.

products.name: The Keeper

economical.note: A direct retail listing for the Keeper Cup, Size A, prices it at $35.00.

accessibility.note: The Keeper is made of natural rubber latex, which rules it out for anyone with a latex allergy; that is a harder constraint than a fit preference, since none of the other cups here are latex.

health.note: FDA's 510(k) database lists K870803, The Keeper Co., 'THE KEEPER', decided substantially equivalent on 1987-05-06 under product code HHE, the oldest clearance in this roster. A direct retail listing confirms the material as natural rubber latex.

products.description: The oldest device in this roster, individually FDA-cleared in 1987 and still made of natural rubber latex rather than silicone, which rules it out for anyone with a latex allergy.

products.name: SckoonCup

economical.note: Sckoon's own site lists the Beginner's Choice SckoonCup at $38.99.

accessibility.note: The brand markets this as a softer, extra-flexible cup aimed at first-time users, which trades some firmness for an easier initial fold and insertion.

health.note: FDA's 510(k) database lists K120107, Sckoon, Inc., 'SCKOONCUP', decided substantially equivalent on 2012-09-18 under product code HHE. Sckoon's own site states the cup is made in the USA of 100% medical-grade silicone.

products.description: A US-made silicone cup marketed as extra soft for first-time users, individually FDA-cleared in 2012.

products.name: Sunny Cup + Applicator

economical.note: Sunny's own site prices the Cup + Applicator at $49.00.

accessibility.note: The applicator is built to insert the cup like a tampon, which the brand markets as easier for a first-time user than folding and inserting a cup by hand. As of the date checked, the brand's own product page listed it as out of stock with a waitlist rather than available to buy.

health.note: FDA's 510(k) database lists K233361, Menstrual Mates, 'Sunny Cup and Applicator', decided substantially equivalent on 2024-06-21 under product code HHE, the newest clearance in this roster.

products.description: The newest device in this roster, FDA-cleared in 2024 with the first tampon-style applicator built into a reusable cup; as of the date checked the brand's own site listed it as out of stock with a waitlist.

products.name: Saalt Cup

economical.note: Saalt's own site prices the Saalt Cup at $32.

accessibility.note: Two sizes are sold, Regular for normal to heavy flow or after childbirth and Small for light to normal flow or first-time users.

health.note: FDA's device registration and listing data show Saalt, LLC registered under product code HHE ('Cup, Menstrual'), listing 'Saalt Cup' among its proprietary names, without an individually numbered 510(k) filing of its own. Saalt's own product page states the cup is 100% medical-grade silicone, free of BPA, latex and toxins.

ethics.note: B Lab's Certified B Corporation directory page for Saalt, LLC shows an overall B Impact Score of 85.8, above the 80-point minimum required for certification.

products.description: A two-size silicone cup from a Certified B Corporation, registered with the FDA under the same device type as individually cleared cups rather than under its own 510(k) number.

products.name: Saalt Disc

economical.note: Saalt's own site prices the Saalt Disc at $35.

accessibility.note: The disc sits behind the pubic bone rather than using suction, and Saalt's own page markets it for use during period sex, with up to 12 hours of wear; a person still needs the same internal-insertion comfort as with a cup.

health.note: FDA's device registration and listing data show Saalt, LLC registered under product code HHE ('Cup, Menstrual'), which also covers menstrual discs, listing 'Saalt Disc' among its proprietary names, without an individually numbered 510(k) filing of its own. Saalt's own product page states the disc is 100% medical-grade silicone, odor free, biocompatible, and free of BPA, latex and toxins.

ethics.note: B Lab's Certified B Corporation directory page for Saalt, LLC shows an overall B Impact Score of 85.8, above the 80-point minimum required for certification.

products.description: A silicone disc from the same B Corp maker as the Saalt Cup, positioned at the cervix instead of using suction and marketed for use during period sex.

products.name: nixit Menstrual Disc

economical.note: nixit's own site prices the disc at $42.00.

accessibility.note: The disc is one size, molds to the body, and holds up to 12 hours without suction; nixit's own page rates it for about 5 years of reuse, shorter than the roughly 10 years several cup makers here claim, so it needs replacing sooner.

health.note: Health Canada's medical device licence data show two active licences for Nixit Limited (first licensed 2020-04-10 and 2024-02-01). FDA's device registration and listing data separately show Nixit Limited registered under product code HHE ('Cup, Menstrual'). nixit's own page states the disc is 100% medical-grade silicone and BPA-free.

products.description: A one-size silicone disc made in Canada, licensed by Health Canada and registered with the FDA; the brand rates it for about five years of reuse, shorter than the roughly ten years claimed for most cups here.

products.name: Flex Reusable Disc

economical.note: Flex's own site prices the Reusable Disc at $34.99.

accessibility.note: Flex's own page describes the disc as designed to fit most vaginas without a size choice, folding to about the size of a tampon for insertion.

health.note: FDA's device registration and listing data show The Flex Company registered under product code HHE ('Cup, Menstrual'), listing 'Flex Reusable Disc' among its proprietary names, without an individually numbered 510(k) filing of its own. Flex's own page states the disc is 100% medical-grade silicone, ISO 10993-tested, and free of BPA, phthalates and natural rubber latex.

products.description: A one-size silicone disc registered with the FDA, with ISO 10993 biocompatibility testing named on the brand's own product page.

products.name: Lena Cup

economical.note: Lena's own site prices the Lena Original at $29.90.

accessibility.note: Lena sells two sizes (Small, Large) and two firmness levels (Original, Sensitive), so a buyer picks both dimensions before ordering.

health.note: FDA's device registration and listing data show a Lena Cup entry registered under product code HHE ('Cup, Menstrual'). Lena's own page states the cup is made in the USA of 100% medical-grade silicone, BPA-free, latex-free and toxin-free, and describes itself as FDA-registered.

products.description: A US-made two-size, two-firmness silicone cup registered with the FDA.

products.name: Pixie Cup

economical.note: Pixie's own site prices the Large Period Cup at $27, on sale at $21 on the date checked.

accessibility.note: Pixie sells two sizes with a standard removal stem and no additional fit customization or applicator.

health.note: FDA's device registration and listing data show a Pixie Cup entry (also listed as 'Dot Cup') registered under product code HHE ('Cup, Menstrual'). Pixie's own page states the cup is medical-grade silicone.

ethics.note: Pixie's own site states that for every cup purchased, a cup is donated free to someone in need, and that the program has passed 135,000 cups donated.

products.description: A two-size silicone cup sold with a buy-one-give-one program the brand says has passed 135,000 cups donated.

products.name: Intimina Lily Cup Compact

economical.note: Intimina's own site lists the Lily Cup Compact at $32.95.

accessibility.note: Intimina's own page describes this as the first collapsible menstrual cup, folding flat into a case for a bag or pocket; it is rated for up to 8 hours of wear, shorter than the 12 hours several other cups and discs here claim, so it needs emptying more often.

health.note: FDA's device registration and listing data show an Intimina entry, filed through Unboxed Inc., registered under product code HHE ('Cup, Menstrual'). Intimina's own product page states the cup is 100% medical-grade silicone.

products.description: The only cup here that folds flat into a case for travel and storage; the brand rates it for eight hours of wear against twelve for most of the others.
